messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate detected in eu-west-2 — STS/IMDS egress showing 5xx spikes; affected services: hosted API (edge auth path) and several Dedicated pools. Trigger: error-rate > 15% over 2m. Pager priority: P1. https://grafana.redwood.example/d/alerts/3342101024

sam (eng-oncall): acked. looking at graphs now. can someone paste the quickquery for token failures?

maria (sre): digging — initial look shows STS latency/5xx spike starting ~3342100600. sustained 5xx on call to sts.amazonaws.com from our auth-proxy. Datadog error-count up ~38% in the last 5m for eu-west-2.

kevin (infra): confirming egress logs — observed increases in 502/504 from the upstream STS endpoint. Some clients hit a TCP reset pattern.

sam (eng-oncall): customer impact? are Dedicated pools returning 5xx or is it only auth failures causing downstream 5xx?

jess (dedicated-ops): Dedicated pools show elevated 5xx when fresh token fetch required: token-cache misses trigger STS calls. Pools with warm cache are fine. Approximated impact: ~22% of requests to Dedicated in eu-west-2 see auth errors leading to 502/503. Hosted API customers in eu-west-2 also seeing increased latency and 5xx.

ash (support): tickets starting to trickle in — two customers reported errors, both in EU region. Flagging for CSOps.

sam (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) switch auth-proxy to fallback token-service (cached internal tokens) 2) route auth calls to eu-west-1 using policy 3) increase retry/backoff to avoid hammering STS. thoughts?

maria (sre): do 1 + 3 immediately. fallback tokens reduce STS dependence and buys time. we should also enable region failover policy for new token requests only.

kevin (infra): agree. I'm rolling a config to auth-proxy now to enable cached-token-mode in eu-west-2 env. Command: 

```
kubectl -n auth-proxy set env deployment/auth-proxy TOKEN_FALLBACK_MODE=cached
kubectl -n auth-proxy rollout restart deployment/auth-proxy
```

kevin (infra): started rollout — 3 pods updated, 3/6 still pending.

sam (eng-oncall): enabling exponential backoff for STS calls in auth-proxy config as well. patching live: 

```
# snippet
retry.max_attempts=5
retry.backoff.initial_ms=200
retry.backoff.multiplier=2.5
```

jess (dedicated-ops): I'm switching Dedicated pool token prewarm to aggressive mode (increase cache TTL for active clients) — will prevent fetches for the next ~10m.

maria (sre): alert: after config rollout, STS call volume dropped ~60% from our auth-proxies in eu-west-2. Error rate dropping but still elevated. latency to STS still high — mean 700ms.

incident-bot: System note: on-call handoff scheduled. sam -> maria in 30m if still ongoing.

sam (eng-oncall): posting customer-facing slack/ops note draft: "We're investigating elevated errors in eu-west-2 caused by an AWS STS degradation; mitigation in progress including cached token fallback and regional failover. Some requests may see increased latency or errors. We'll update in 15m." any edits?

ash (support): looks good, add a note we are prioritizing Dedicated customers with SLAs.

oliver (product): add: we're monitoring for potential data plane retries causing higher cost; will notify if we expect prolonged mitigation window.

maria (sre): next steps: monitor error rate, open case with AWS for STS in eu-west-2. kevin, can you open a support case and attach egress traces?

kevin (infra): opening AWS case now — case# 1234567890. pasted link to case: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/1234567890

jess (dedicated-ops): Dedicated pool manual routing: if auth continues to fail, we have a plan to route new sessions to eu-west-1 Dedicated pool (config change, <5m deploy). prepping the runbook.

sam (eng-oncall): execute customer mitigation checklist: 1) Set status page to degraded (done?) 2) Post to status with region-specific note 3) Notify account owners for impacted customers.

ash (support): status page update pushed: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/3342101024

maria (sre): AWS reply: "We are investigating increased error rates on STS in eu-west-2 caused by elevated control plane load; engineering is engaged" — updated in case notes.

kevin (infra): observed partial improvement: STS 5xx down to ~8% error rate, auth-proxy errors dropping, hosted API 5xx trending down.

sam (eng-oncall): good. keep monitoring. Maria, if AWS doesn't restore within 20m let's run the regional failover for new token requests and prepare for full session routing if needed.

maria (sre): agreed. also enabling enhanced logging for failed token fetches to collect traces for AWS. adding a temporary sampling rule in prod: 

```
# datadog: trace sampling
service: auth-proxy
env: prod
sample_rate: 100
filter: "resource.name:GET /token"
```

jess (dedicated-ops): Dedicated reroute plan stands by. prepping announcement to customers on 10m warning before active reroute.

incident-bot: Reminder: on-call escalation timer 25m. Next: if error rate > 10% after 25m -> escalate to eng-leads.

ash (support): adding two customers to high-touch: AccountA (SLA enterprise), AccountB (mid-market). sending DMs to account owners now.

kevin (infra): AWS update: partial mitigation implemented on their side; they've added capacity for STS in eu-west-2 and are watching. case updated.

maria (sre): metrics are steadying. hosted API 5xx baseline returning to normal, Dedicated pools still slightly elevated but within acceptable window after token-cache changes.

sam (eng-oncall): taking this to monitoring phase. leaving a note for handoff: please keep case open until AWS confirms root cause and we see two 30m windows of normal error rates. maria taking next on-call.

maria (sre): taking over. I'll keep this thread updated.

ash (support): closing high-touch alert for AccountB — they confirm stability. AccountA on call still monitoring.

oliver (product): capture learnings: need a TTL-boost toggle and cross-region token fallback in playbooks. adding to product backlog.

maria (sre): postmortem bits: cause = AWS STS egress/control-plane degradation in eu-west-2 -> amplified by token-cache misses. Mitigations applied: cached-token fallback, increased token prewarm, retry/backoff, temporary region failover readiness. Action items: 1) add cached-token-mode to runbook 2) automatic cached-token fallback when STS error-rate > 5% 3) add cross-region routing test 4) update SLAs comms.

sam (eng-oncall): thanks team. incident moved to monitoring/cleanup. will reopen if regressions. :thumbsup:
